items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: it features ten piano players — Hank Jones, John Lewis, Kenny Barron, Ray Bryant, Gene Harris, Joanne Brackeen, Roger Kellaway, and who have I left out, oh, Cedar Walton and myself.

ctx.x: Which we have with us today for your autograph.

But I’m contracted to Enja now. And I just got back from Japan on a tour that is called “100 Gold Fingers,” it features ten piano players — Hank Jones, John Lewis, Kenny Barron, Ray Bryant, Gene Harris, Joanne Brackeen, Roger Kellaway, and who have I left out, oh, Cedar Walton and myself. And there was one more. Ten of us.

items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: And Cedar Walton, they put us together to do duos and it was a lot of fun. Junior Mance, the Blues Brothers, Ray Bryant, Roger Kellaway.

ctx.x: Yeah. And I think it was 1995, I guess that’s when it was, I was the token woman. That was great. It was great. We played quite a few concerts in Japan and we went to Korea and then I had my own concert in China, so I just made a nice little debut around there. It was great. We had Hank Jones and Kenny Barron and John Lewis. I’d never really hung out with these people, my idols from when I first started listening to music. And Cedar Walton, they put us together to do duos and it was a lot of fun. Junior Mance,…
I’d like to hear you and Roger together actually.
